swap_risks: CRITICAL OP-AMP VS COMPARATOR TRAP: TLV3201AIDBVR is a comparator with push-pull output while TLV9001IDBVR is a opamp with push-pull output. Even with identical pinouts, an open-collector comparator CANNOT pull high without an external pull-up resistor and lacks internal Miller compensation — dropping it into a linear negative-feedback op-amp circuit causes severe oscillation; conversely, using an op-amp as a comparator causes slow overdrive recovery and output saturation lag.
BENCH VERIFICATION: Confirm thermal dissipation margin using θJA (TLV3201AIDBVR: 237.8 °C/W vs TLV9001IDBVR: 232.9 °C/W) and worst-case ambient temperature (-40..125 °C vs -40..125 °C).
engineering_verdict: TLV3201AIDBVR (Texas Instruments, SOT-23-5) and TLV9001IDBVR (Texas Instruments, SOT-23-5) are Level 2 Functional / Tuning Required replacements: while the footprint is physically compatible, engineering review and passive/circuit adjustments are mandatory due to device kind / output stage mismatch (comparator/push-pull vs opamp/push-pull). Key datasheet deltas: device type is comparator (push-pull) vs opamp (push-pull), supply limit is 5.5 V (p.4) vs 5.5 V (p.14), max Vos is 3 mV (p.5) vs 1.6 mV (p.17), input bias current is 1 pA (p.5) vs 5 pA (p.17), and Iq/ch is 40 µA (p.5) vs 60 µA (p.18). Always validate pinout orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.7), thermal margin (θJA 237.8 vs 232.9 °C/W), and official manufacturer datasheets on hardware prototypes before production release.
